primary_diagnosis_treated: Unstable atherosclerotic coronary disease (non‑STEMI acute coronary syndrome)

medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG185 recommends low‑dose aspirin 75 mg OD for all IHD patients (lifelong)
NICE CG126 advises aspirin plus a P2Y12 inhibitor (prasugrel) for 12 months post‑ACS

medications.purpose: Anti‑anginal, heart‑rate control and mortality reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists beta‑blocker as first‑line anti‑anginal (target HR 55‑60 bpm)

medications.purpose: Cardioprotective antihypertensive for IHD and hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126/NG136 recommends ACE‑I for all IHD patients and for hypertension control

medications.purpose: Intensive LDL‑C lowering for secondary prevention
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 recommends high‑intensity statin (atorvastatin 80 mg) for all IHD patients
NICE CG126 acute management advises enoxaparin during ACS admission

medications.purpose: Add‑on anti‑anginal if chest pain persists despite beta‑blocker
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG126 lists long‑acting nitrate as second‑line anti‑anginal therapy

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined statins increase risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis (CYP3A4 competition)
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue simvastatin and pravastatin before initiating atorvastatin

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive anticoagulant effect raises bleeding risk
interactions_checked.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; avoid concurrent NSAIDs
Start nitrate at low dose, check blood pressure and symptoms after 48‑72 h

interactions_checked.interaction: Risk of electrolyte disturbances (K⁺) and renal function changes
interactions_checked.action: Check electrolytes and renal function 1‑2 weeks after dose change; consider stopping the combination tablet

assumptions_warnings: Allergy status not provided – verify no allergy to aspirin, statins, ACE‑I, or beta‑blocker before initiating new drugs.
Blood pressure and heart‑rate readings not available – obtain measurements before titrating lisinopril or metoprolol.
LVEF not documented – MRA or ARNI not started until echocardiogram confirms HFrEF.
HbA1c not available – assess glycaemic status to guide diabetes management.
Smoking status unknown – address smoking cessation as part of non‑pharmacological plan.
Renal function (eGFR 66 mL/min) is acceptable for standard enoxaparin dosing, but monitor anti‑Xa if eGFR falls <30 mL/min.
treatment_summary: The patient is already on aspirin, prasugrel, metoprolol, lisinopril/HCTZ and low‑intensity statins. Replace simvastatin and pravastatin with high‑intensity atorvastatin 80 mg, simplify ACE‑I therapy to lisinopril 30 mg daily, continue existing antiplatelet and beta‑blocker regimens, add short‑course enoxaparin for the acute NSTEMI, and consider isosorbide mononitrate if angina persists. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, CK, BP, HR, and bleeding signs per NICE CG126 and NG136.
